what_this_is: The Workshop row for the still-image and thumbnail compositor that runs on the person's computer.

payload.label: Build thumbnail candidates and still images from my frames (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Make thumbnails from six fixed layouts, or make still images from my own canvas, frame, shape and text settings.
payload.description: Each candidate uses either a scene or one of the six 1280x720 layouts: split_claim, face_right_stack, zoom_flaw, tags, hold_quote, corner_face. A scene sets its canvas width, height and background and paints ordered image, rect and text layers. An image layer center-crops a named PNG to cover its box. A rect layer fills its box. A text layer fits copy in its box with the person's font. Both kinds of candidate write one RGB PNG with the candidate ID as its name.

request.description: Path to a JSON file on the person's computer. Give out and candidates from settings.candidates or the settings_record itself. Use only to select IDs. A scene candidate is {scene: {width, height, background, layers}}. Each layer has type and box {x, y, width, height}: image needs frame; rect needs paint; text needs paint, text, font_size and can set min_font_size or font_style. Give frames if using images and font {file, variable} if using text. Legacy candidates use {template, ...values} and still require frames, cutouts and font. See the README for limits and legacy values.

output_schema.description: The last line: {"result": {"thumbnails": [paths]}} or {"error": what to change}.

invoke.say: Run from the root of the Workshop checkout on the person's computer. Use the person's settings record or give the requested candidates in settings.candidates. Use the person's existing frames and font. Pass the request file path as {request}. Name the PNGs written or say what the error asks to change. If you cannot run commands, give the person these steps.

provenance.source: Ported from a film's thumbnail builder: its layout functions are the templates; its candidate table is the person's settings row
